absent: No test or receipt couples the reviewed test to the product's neighbour combine: the test defines and exercises its own _max_scatter helper and calls only _carrier_adjacency from the product, so a change to the product's combine at contour_tree.py:326 is invisible to it.

No negative control mutates the product. The run's negative control rewrites the test file's own _max_scatter in a scratch copy, so it demonstrates the test detects changes to itself, not that the guard fires on a product defect.

findings.text: follow-on: the test does not exercise the product's combine, so it pins a jax.numpy identity rather than the behaviour its docstring names ('The carrier neighbour combine is a duplicate-index maximum scatter'). _max_scatter (line 44, identity.at[keys].max(values)) is defined in the test file; the only product symbol the module imports is _carrier_adjacency (line 20), used for an order assertion on the saturated case. The product contains no maximum scatter at all: `grep -n '.max(' nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py` returns only jnp.max at lines 257 and 437 (rank reductions), and there is no segment_max. The duplicate carrier keys the evidence names are combined last-write-wins at parents.at[neighbour_root].set(...) (contour_tree.py:326), and _carrier_adjacency itself writes slots with .set. So the three assertions in _assert_agrees (scatter == segment_max, compare bytes; then segmented == numpy np.maximum.at) hold for any JAX version regardless of what nova does, and the test would not fail if the product's combine changed. The run's evidence_inputs acknowledges the product site is .set but the test never reaches it. The correct pin for the product is the same-value invariant the .set combine relies on (duplicate keys carry identical values, so last-write-wins equals a maximum); the test's data inverts that, feeding distinct values to duplicate keys (the saturated case uses arange(32,0,-1) on key 0), which is exactly the input on which .set and .max differ.

follow-on: the negative control mutates the test module, not the product, so it does not demonstrate that the guard fires on the defect it claims to guard. The scratch tree is /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261002T233222856971-ctta-scatter-segmented-max-equivalence/neg-control.BuHUsw and the mutated module_under_test named on line 3 is .../neg-control.BuHUsw/tests/test_contour_tree_scatter_equivalence.py, with nova imported unchanged from the reviewed worktree via PYTHONPATH. The six failures (FAILED .../neg-control.BuHUsw/tests/test_contour_tree_scatter_equivalence.py::test_saturated_vertex_combine_matches_segment_max and ...::test_random_carrier_endpoint_scatter_matches_segment_max[0..4]) land inside the scratch test's own _max_scatter/_assert_agrees, confirming the test detects a change to its own helper. Because the product's combine is never invoked, no product-side mutation could make this test fail; the negative control therefore measures the helper, not the subject.

follow-on: the evidence fragment's mechanism narrative states the product combines duplicates with a maximum ('Combining duplicates with a maximum removes that dependence', line 7; 'the equivalence holds because the combine is a maximum', line 28; 'This node names the equivalence the sweep relies on', line 8), but the product does not use a maximum combine: the sole site the reviewed manifest's evidence_inputs cites, contour_tree.py:326, is parents.at[neighbour_root].set(...), last-write-wins, and the sweep's safety rests on an equality invariant (neighbour slots sharing a root are in the same union-find component and carry the same value vertex), argued in the earlier sweep review rather than pinned here. The fragment's claim is therefore true of the test's helper and false of the code path, so a reader who takes the fragment at its word believes a maximum scatter is guarded in noumenal code where none exists.

justifications.evidence: The gate reproduces: I re-ran the committed file with JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu against the shared environment and measured 8 passed in 13.79s, EXIT=0 (run dir review-gate-after.log), matching the run's 35.02s 8-passed gate-head.log. The negative control also reproduces (6 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1). But neither log supports the deliverable's claim: the negative control mutates the test, not the product, so it shows only that the test is sensitive to its own helper; and because the product contains no maximum scatter and the test imports only _carrier_adjacency, a product mutation could not move either log. The evidence therefore under-determines the claim it is offered for.

The evidence fragment is scoped under the plan's contour-tree-topology-authority directory as the plan's evidence convention requires. justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's stated goal is to pin the carrier neighbour duplicate-index maximum scatter equivalence with a committed test, naming followup f-ctta-sweep-durability-and-placement item (4). It delivered a passing eight-case gate with a matching negative control and committed both the test and the evidence. The goal is only partly met, however: the test's subject is a test-local helper, the product uses last-write-wins .set at the site the node itself cites (contour_tree.py:326), and the test's data feeds distinct values to duplicate keys, inverting the equality invariant that makes the product's .set safe. So the test names an equivalence that the product does not use and could not use as the test poses it, and it would not catch a regression in the product's combine.
justifications.scope_discipline: The two commits touch exactly two files, tests/test_contour_tree_scatter_equivalence.py and docs/evidence/fragments/contour-tree-topology-authority/ctta-scatter-segmented-max-equivalence.html, both inside the reviewed node's declared write paths; the product file is untouched, consistent with the manifest note that peer node ctta-carrier-adjacency-index-dtype owns it. The reviewed worktree is clean at the reviewed head. The manifest records a check-manifest self-audit returning ok=false ('changed paths outside the write scope') despite the live pointer's node.write_paths carrying the same two paths; that is a node-resolution discrepancy in the audit, not a stray write, and the run surfaced it under follow_ons rather than hiding it.
